verses.1: As for the spiritual matters, brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant of them.
verses.2: You know that when people were tribes, they would avoid those strange and unfamiliar things like the plague.
verses.3: Therefore, I know that no one who speaks from the Spirit of God can say, “Anathema to Jesus!” Nor can anyone say, “Lord Jesus, isn’t You truly divine?”
verses.4: Divisions of talents are indeed necessary; but that same spirit is also important.
verses.5: And there are also divisions based on months; and he himself is the Lord.
verses.6: And there are also divisions in actions; yet he alone is God, who does everything throughout all things.
verses.7: To each person, however, the manifestation of the spirit is given according to their needs.
verses.8: For indeed, wisdom is given through the spirit; another kind of knowledge is given by the same spirit.
verses.9: One trust in that same spirit; other gifts of blessings in that same spirit.
verses.10: Another are the actions of armies; another is prophecy; another are the distinctions between breaths. Another is the origin of languages; another is the interpretation of languages.
verses.11: But all of these things are carried out by that One Spirit, who divides each one separately according to His will.
verses.12: For just as the body has many parts and members, so too, in the body, all of its parts are numerous. Similarly, Christ also has many aspects/parts.
verses.13: For in one spirit, we all have been baptized into one body, whether we are Jews or Greeks, slaves or free people. All of us are united by one spirit.
verses.14: For indeed, the body is not a single entity, but rather it consists of many parts.
verses.15: If he says that: But isn’t it not from the body? It isn’t from the flesh. It doesn’t come from the body at all.
verses.16: And if he says those things… But I’m not an eye; I don’t come from the body. It doesn’t come from the body at all.
verses.17: If the entire body is an eye, then where is hearing? If everything is hearing, then where is sight?
verses.18: But now, the Lord placed each member in its proper place, in its own body, as He desired.
verses.19: And if everything were one single part, then where would the body be?
verses.20: Now, there are many members, but they form one whole.
verses.21: But the eye cannot speak through its fingers. I have no use for your hands; nor do I have any use for your heads either. I have no use for you at all.
verses.22: But more importantly, the members of the body must be weaker in order to function properly.
verses.23: And what we consider to be more honorable for the body, we should give greater respect to it. And those things that are dishonorable to us, they have more dignity than anything else.
verses.24: But those things that are not beneficial to us are unnecessary. Instead, God honored the body more by giving it even more respect.
verses.25: So that no cracks may appear in the body; instead, its parts should be able to fit together perfectly with each other.
verses.26: And whether one member suffers, all members suffer together; and whether one member is honored, all members rejoice together.
verses.27: We are, therefore, the body of Christ, and we are members of His body.
verses.28: And those whom God first appointed in the church were apostles, then prophets, then teachers. After that came those who had authority over others, those who could bring about enlightenment, those who could govern others. Then there were those who could speak various languages.
verses.29: Not all apostles were so; not all prophets were like that; not all teachers were also such. Not all people had power or authority either.
verses.30: Do not all gifts have their own meanings? Do not all languages speak in a certain way? Do not all interpretations be made?
verses.31: Also, be careful with the larger gifts. I’m still giving you excessive hints about this.
